specific_objectives: 6.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to describe types of corrosion.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Visual inspection of corrosion samples; Safety: Wear gloves and eye protection; Supervision: Instructor monitors handling of samples
intro_questions: What is the primary purpose of aircraft husbandry?
Why is regular maintenance essential for aircraft safety?
Can you list three factors that degrade aircraft structures?

development.content:
Definition of aircraft husbandry
Importance of structural integrity
Impact of environmental factors
Role of scheduled maintenance
Consequences of neglecting husbandry

Types of corrosion mechanisms
Galvanic corrosion principles
Environmental corrosion factors
Internal vs external corrosion
Effect of moisture and salts

Preventive measures against corrosion
Inspection techniques for corrosion
Documentation of corrosion findings
Reporting procedures for defects
Basic cleaning and preservation methods

summary_questions: Explain the difference between galvanic and environmental corrosion.
How does neglecting husbandry affect aircraft operational safety?
What are the key steps in reporting a corrosion defect?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the specific corrosion types discussed in this lesson and how they relate to the definition of corrosion on steel, aluminum, and magnesium alloys covered in LP 02.

pft_rows.syllabus: Definition of corrosion on steel products, aluminum and magnesium alloys and copper alloys.
